About this item

  • COMPLETE BEGINNER GUITAR KIT: Start playing with a 30-inch junior classical guitar, travel and storage gig bag, detachable shoulder strap, spare nylon strings, guitar picks and cleaning cloth for lessons, practice and recitals
  • JUNIOR 1/4-SIZE DESIGN: Compact 30-inch guitar is easier for young beginners to hold and control, making it a practical starter instrument for children learning chords, strumming, finger placement and basic technique

  • HANDCRAFTED WOOD CONSTRUCTION: Linden wood body, birch headstock, dyed hardwood fingerboard, protective binding, decorative rosette and high-gloss polished body and back create a traditional classical appearance

Product Description

Help a new musician begin playing with the Pyle PGACLS30 Beginner Acoustic Guitar Kit. This compact 30-inch junior classical guitar combines a traditional body shape with a comfortable 1/4-size design suitable for children, students and beginning players. The six-string guitar features nylon strings that provide a comfortable playing feel while beginners learn notes, basic chords, strumming patterns and finger placement. Its handcrafted wooden construction includes a linden wood body, birch wood headstock, dyed hardwood fingerboard, protective body binding, decorative rosette and a polished high-gloss finish. Chrome 3-in-line tuning machines provide convenient string adjustment, while the 18-fret fingerboard and 19.7-inch scale length support lessons, home practice, recitals and beginner music programs. The compact dimensions also make the guitar easier to store and transport than a full-size instrument. The complete starter set includes a travel and storage gig bag, detachable shoulder strap, spare nylon guitar strings, guitar picks and a cleaning cloth, giving new players the essential accessories needed to begin practicing. Total Guitar Length: 30 inches Scale Length: 19.7 inches or 500 millimeters Body Length: 14.4 inches or 365 millimeters Neck Length, Nut to Body: 16.1 inches or 410 millimeters Number of Frets: 18 Body Material: Linden wood Headstock Material: Birch wood Fingerboard Material: Dyed hardwood String Material: Nylon Overall Dimensions: 30.5 by 11.2 by 2.8 inches Package Contents: 30-inch classical guitar Travel and storage gig bag Detachable shoulder strap Spare nylon guitar strings Guitar picks Cleaning cloth

    5 out of 5 stars
    Very complete and inexpensive beginner set
    My 6 year old son has been learning violin for more than half a year. I wanted to get him a cheap guitar, since it is relatively easy to learn it for violin players. He is 50" tall, so this 30" guitar was the right size. For how inexpensive it is, I was very happy with this guitar. It feels solid and well built, and it has good sound. I used the digital tuner included with the guitar and was able to tune it, I only had some trouble with the 6th string until I figured out that I had to play it repeatedly while tuning for the tuner to catch the note properly. Once tuned, the guitar puts out a decent sound, and my son is very excited to learn to play it. I like that it comes with the shoulder strap and case. The picks are the only thing that feels a little cheap; they work ok, but they are very thin plastic Overall, this is definitely a "low tier", beginner guitar, but it is great to get such a complete set so cheap. That way we can test if my son is interested on learning it alongside with the violin, without having to invest a lot of money on it.

      Works well for the price. Playability is great as it can make sound fairly well. Going down the fret board it starts to be off from what the tone should be in general but this still makes a good starting point to where if you have a kid that wants to try guitar start out.

      You'll need to always tune every time at the beginning of playing as it become out of tune even after a day. The material is ok and wish there was more rigid material or epoxy used in order to stiffen it up as I'm pretty sure this is what is contributing to the need to tune every time you play.

      Material and Pickup quality is good as it reverberates well making a good round sound. I believe there should be better glue/epoxy that could be used where the neck it as it's only been about 6 months since I bought and can notice there's cracking around the neck. So only time will tell when the next breaks but this could also contribute to the need to retune every session.

      Great guitar for small fingers to get into it and then moving on to a better one in order to find something more long lasting.

      4 out of 5 stars
      Pretty Good Beginner Guitar That’s Fun For Any Skill Level
      Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2024
      Color: 5) Onyx
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      So I really like this guitar! It has a hard plastic (or something similar) body that feels very solid and feels like it will last a long time as well. It has a really deep resonate tone as well. I chose the 30” version because I also have a KALA Baritone Ukelele and a Yamaha Guitalele. This one is pretty close in size to the KALA Baritone Uke, and quite a bit bigger than the Guitalele. But it sounds very much as loud and deep as a standard sized guitar. Its nylon strings are comfortable on the fingers and the neck is straight and overall is pretty well setup. My main concern with it is that the action is just too high to easily play. I can’t imagine how a novice would enjoy playing this. It takes a different amount of pressure to fret a note at the first fret than it does at the 12th. Or the 5th even. Or the 2nd actually. My plan is to lower the action at the bridge. The string height at the first fret/nut is actually reall good. I have some (a little) experience working on banjos and the “repair” I have to perform is fairly minimal. Even so, I have the proper tools to modify the bridge and to accurately measure the action as I go along. So I feel very comfortable making this change.

      Now, the question for you is: Was the 30” version I got the same as all other 30” in terms of string height? My guess is probably so. Is the larger size versions of this guitar the same as a the smallest size in that the action will be too high? I’m going to hazard a guess and say no. As the size goes up, especially, I would think the action would be much better. That actually occurred to me when I chose the 30” but I wanted one to practice with and tool around on that was about the same size as my other small instruments. It makes it easier to switch from one to the other when the sizes are more consistent. And besides, I am learning to play mandolin as well and the strings of a mandolin are very close together and very close to the fret board,, so I wanted to keep the guitar action closer to that so practice on one would transfer to practice on the mandolin. Overall I like this guitar very much! It is fun to play, even with the high string action. When I lower the strings, it will be about as perfect (for me) as a small inexpensive guitar can be. Oh, meant to add also that this is light years in quality beyond those crappy little toy guitars you find at Walmart.

      Very well made child's musical instrument. Holds its tune, unlike other small beginner guitars.
      Reviewed in the United States on April 6, 2024
      Color: 2) Ash, Gloss
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      Very pleased with this guitar that is very well made. It includes the truss and truss adjustment that stabilizes the neck against the stretch of the guitar strings, so that it holds its tune. It is a musical instrument - not a frustrating toy for a beginning learner. The included tuner works for all of the notes. This was not so for a competitor we purchased and returned since it was poorly made and didn't hold a tune at all!) I ordered replacement strings from a music store, since another reviewer suggested that. But, so far we are happy with the strings that it came with. After buying the cheaper one, I delved further into research for a child's guitar and found this was recommended by a true guitar manufacturer. A big brand name was twice the cost or more, which wasn't reasonable for what may be a passing interest for our grandchild. It is not a small "parlor" guitar for an adult, but has the smaller neck and fret length for small child's hands. Very nice tone given the small size. We have not used the online lessons, since we will let our son set that up but that's a nice extra.

      5 out of 5 stars
      Nice quality beginner guitar
      Reviewed in the United States on April 2, 2025
      Color: 3) Black, Matte
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      This 1/4 size guitar is nice quality for young beginners to learn on. It is a scaled down version of a full size guitar and I like that it doesn’t make any compromises on components. Many beginner guitars have plastic or otherwise cheap feeling parts, they don’t hold a tune and don’t sound terrific. This guitar feels great in hand and sounds warm and really nice. It has nylon strings which are more beginner friendly than metal ones, being more comfortable to play. They take a couple more days to break in but hold tune just fine after that. The guitar comes with an extra set of strings which is handy. Overall a nice guitar for little kids to learn on before they can handle a full or even half size guitar.

      We purchased this to see if our 5 year old would stick with guitar before buying a more expensive instrument. This is decent enough for what we purchased it for. If you care about quality this is not for you. Parts of the guitar were dinged and paint scratched off sound is not great but good enough if you’re testing out a new learners interest. THERE IS NO MUSIC CLASS SUBSCRIPTION! I partially ordered this guitar over a slightly cheaper one because that is what they advertised. When I went to redeem my subscription they told me it’s actually a $40.00 coupon and can only be used once - that means you can only purchase ONE lesson. If the lesson costs less than 40.00 the balance of the money is forfeited by you. So if you take a $2.00 group lesson you lose the rest of the $38.00. This is not a two month music lesson subscription by any means. When I confronted the company about it showing the flyer that came with the guitar they did not respond back.

    • Ryott
      5 out of 5 stars
      Very complete and inexpensive beginner set
      Reviewed in the United States on March 23, 2019
      Color: 2) Ash, Gloss
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      My 6 year old son has been learning violin for more than half a year. I wanted to get him a cheap guitar, since it is relatively easy to learn it for violin players. He is 50" tall, so this 30" guitar was the right size.

      For how inexpensive it is, I was very happy with this guitar. It feels solid and well built, and it has good sound. I used the digital tuner included with the guitar and was able to tune it, I only had some trouble with the 6th string until I figured out that I had to play it repeatedly while tuning for the tuner to catch the note properly.

      Once tuned, the guitar puts out a decent sound, and my son is very excited to learn to play it. I like that it comes with the shoulder strap and case. The picks are the only thing that feels a little cheap; they work ok, but they are very thin plastic

      Overall, this is definitely a "low tier", beginner guitar, but it is great to get such a complete set so cheap. That way we can test if my son is interested on learning it alongside with the violin, without having to invest a lot of money on it.

      1 out of 5 stars
      Feels cheap and sound very average when stock
      Reviewed in the United States on December 28, 2021
      Color: 2) Ash, Gloss
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      Edit: my son didn’t use the guitar and we kept it in the box well protected. Today, my son my finally ready and motivated to play! Great news!

      Or not.. when I realised the guitar cracked from top to middle (by itself) I knew the quality was cheap but I would at least expect a cheap guitar to break after getting smashed.. not in a box somewhere (not even accessible to my 4yo son)

      I bought it for my son to learn guitar and the guitar does feel cheap, light and fragile.

      It sounds pretty bad with the stock strings but once I changed it for the Ernie's, it was ok.

      Keep in mind that the stock strings will also de tune very fast when using it for the first time. You might have to tune it every 5min (4-5 times in a row) for them to stabilize a bit. Or just buy good strings (Around 6usd)
